title: A Past Cause, a Present Result

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know two ways to imagine things with *si*. From B1 Unit 35: *si* + *hubiera* + past participle, with *habría* + participle in the result, imagines a past that did not happen (*Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado*). From B1 Unit 4: *si* + imperfect subjunctive with the conditional imagines the present (*Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría*). A mixed conditional uses one of each. The *si* clause looks back at a past choice that was not made, and the result clause is about now, so the result takes the simple conditional, not *habría* + participle: *Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería médica* means "If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now." I did not study medicine, and I am not a doctor. A past choice can change the present, and each clause uses the tense for its own time.

sections.title: Same condition, two results
rows: Si hubiera estudiado más, habría aprobado el examen.
If I had studied more, I would have passed the exam. (Past result: B1 Unit 35.)
Si hubiera estudiado más, ahora tendría un mejor trabajo.
If I had studied more, I would have a better job now. (Result in the present.)
Si me hubiera mudado al sur, ahora viviría cerca del mar.
If I had moved south, I would live near the sea now.
Si no hubiéramos vendido la casa, hoy tendríamos un jardín.
If we had not sold the house, we would have a garden today.

items.spanish: Si hubiera aceptado aquel empleo, ahora viviría en Lima.
items.english: If I had accepted that job, I would live in Lima now.

items.spanish: Si no nos hubiéramos conocido en la universidad, hoy no estaríamos juntos.
items.english: If we had not met at university, we would not be together today.

items.spanish: Si mis padres no hubieran viajado a Chile, yo no hablaría español.
items.english: If my parents had not travelled to Chile, I would not speak Spanish.

items.spanish: Si hubieras llamado ayer, ahora sabrías la respuesta.
items.english: If you had called yesterday, you would know the answer now.

sections.content: Look at the result clause. A word that points to now, such as *ahora*, *hoy*, *todavía* or *ya*, usually means the simple conditional. If the result belongs to the past too, you are back in the pattern of B1 Unit 35 and need *habría* + participle. English works the same way ("If I had studied, I would be a doctor now"). In the *si* clause, *habría* never appears: say *si hubiera estudiado*, not *si habría estudiado*.
